cases.summary: The GPS trace shows the driver took a materially longer route than the app's reference route: 10,598 m actual vs 7,956 m reference, an excess of 2,642 m (+33.2%), far exceeding the RD-1 materiality threshold of 796 m. The trip also took 418 s longer than the reference estimate and included one unexplained 180-second stop. The rider objected twice in chat (CHAT-01, CHAT-03) and asked the driver to follow the app route, so neither RD-3 (rider approval) nor RD-4 (documented diversion) applies. Under RD-2 the rider is entitled to a refund of the excess-distance charge, computed by the server as S$2.97.

cases.summary: The driver took an alternative route to avoid congestion on the usual expressway, which the driver believed was faster at the time. GPS data shows a material detour under RD-1 (+2642 m, +33.2%, exceeding the 796 m threshold), and the fare charged was S$19.10 with valid arithmetic. The rider objected twice in chat (CHAT-01, CHAT-03), and the driver did not obtain rider approval for the longer route. No documented road closure or navigation reroute is present in the evidence, so RD-4 does not apply. The driver's stated reason (expressway jam) is a plausible operational judgment but is not a policy-recognized exemption. Under RD-2, the eligible excess-distance refund is S$2.97. The driver's position is best served by acknowledging the material deviation while noting the absence of any documented diversion or rider approval, which means the remedy is limited to the computed excess rather than the full fare.
